statements.section: 8. From the scalar formula to one ordinary QAOA word

statements.markdown:
A depth-$p$ state, with $p$ counting cost–mixer pairs, is
$$
|\psi_{n,p,J}(\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta)\rangle
=e^{-i\beta_pB_n}e^{-i\gamma_pC_{n,J}}\cdots
 e^{-i\beta_1B_n}e^{-i\gamma_1C_{n,J}}|+\rangle^{\otimes n}.
$$
Here the real angle vectors $\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta$ are
deterministic; $\boldsymbol\gamma$ is separate from the Parisi coefficient
$\gamma(t)$. A *word* means a finite ordered product of cost and mixer
exponentials. Its pattern and angles are fixed independently of $n,J$;
its cost operator depends on $n,J$. Define
$$
v_p(\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta)
=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\mathbb E_J
 \langle\psi_{n,p,J}|C_{n,J}|\psi_{n,p,J}\rangle,
\qquad Q_p=\sup_{\boldsymbol\gamma,\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^p}v_p.
$$
statements.section: 8. From the scalar formula to one ordinary QAOA word

statements.markdown:
Let $\widehat Z_i,\widehat X_i$ be Pauli operators, and define the cost
and mixer by
$$
C_{n,J}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\widehat Z_i\widehat Z_j,
\qquad B_n=\sum_i\widehat X_i.
$$
The cost eigenvalues are $H_n(\sigma)$. QAOA alternates cost evolution
and mixing from the uniform state $|+\rangle^{\otimes n}$
([Farhi, Goldstone and Gutmann (2014)][FGG]). For a fixed sequence
$W=(\theta_1,\beta_1,\ldots,\theta_p,\beta_p)$, write
$$
|\psi_{n,J}(W)\rangle
=e^{-i\beta_p B_n}e^{-i\theta_p C_{n,J}}\cdots
 e^{-i\beta_1 B_n}e^{-i\theta_1 C_{n,J}}|+\rangle^{\otimes n},
$$
$$
v(W)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\mathbb E_J
\langle\psi_{n,J}(W)|C_{n,J}|\psi_{n,J}(W)\rangle.
$$

lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinHamiltonian
lean.note: Support model. Sum over i<j, divided by the square root of n. The couplings are indexed by all ordered pairs; only i<j enter.

lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinDisorder
lean.note: Support model. Product of standard Gaussians over all ordered pairs, so independence is built into the measure.

statements.markdown:
For each unordered pair choose an independent standard Gaussian
$J_{ij}$, a normal random variable with mean zero and variance one.
Independence means that learning the other couplings does not change
the probability distribution of this one.
These coefficients, or **couplings**, are drawn once and then held
fixed while we maximise the energy, or **Hamiltonian**,

$$
H_n(\sigma)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}J_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j.
$$

develops its circuit construction and
the order of limits.

lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinHamiltonian
lean.note: Support model. Lean encodes each sign as a Boolean, read as +1 or -1 inside the sum.

statements.markdown:
At each of $n$ positions, or **sites**, we choose a sign $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$,
called a **spin**. A configuration is the vector
$\sigma=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n)$.

lean.clause: J (i,j) * (if σ i then 1 else -1) * (if σ j then 1 else -1)
lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.spinHamiltonian
lean.note: Support model. Each term is the coupling times the product of two signs.

statements.markdown:
A positive coupling rewards equal signs; a negative one rewards opposite
signs.

For example, positive couplings on pairs $12$ and $23$ favour
$\sigma_1=\sigma_2=\sigma_3$, which conflicts with a negative coupling
on pair $13$. This inability to maximise every pair's contribution
simultaneously is called **frustration**.
statements.note: Illustration only: frustration has no Lean counterpart.

statements.markdown:
For two spins, $H_2(\sigma)=J_{12}\sigma_1\sigma_2/\sqrt2$.
Choosing equal or opposite signs according to the sign of $J_{12}$ gives
$\max_\sigma H_2(\sigma)=|J_{12}|/\sqrt2$.

lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Heat.heatKernel_formula
lean.note: Support model. The density for variance t; t=1 is this φ. Positivity, total integral and the interval formula come from mathlib's gaussianReal.

statements.markdown:
A **probability density** assigns probability by area. For a standard
Gaussian random variable $Z$, the density is
$\varphi(z)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/2}$; it is nonnegative, has total
integral one, and for $a\le b$ gives

$$
\Pr(a\le Z\le b)=\int_a^b\varphi(z)\,dz.
$$
statements.note: Textbook background. The couplings use mathlib's gaussianReal 0 1, and the Lean writes the density formula for its heat kernel.

statements.markdown:
Thus the expected two-spin maximum is $1/\sqrt\pi$. For any signs
chosen before seeing the coupling, the expected energy is instead zero.
statements.note: No Lean counterpart: the Lean has no two-spin case.

statements.markdown:
The order matters: we choose signs for each realised coupling, then average
the achieved maximum.

The model is **pure** because every term contains
exactly two spins, and has **zero external field** because there is
no additional term $h\sum_i\sigma_i$.
